newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Firmer on tight prompt supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Firmer on tight prompt supplies.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets were stronger on Monday amid tight supplies in March and traders expect the backwardation, where forward months are below the front month, would get steeper.
Traders said if the 500,000 tonnes of arbitrage cargoes from the west did arrive in Asia during late March/early April, it would have a bearish effect on prices in April.

But this would be balanced by the supply cutback resulting from the shutdown of Mobil Oil Singapore's 282,000-bpd refinery from mid-March, and Singapore Refining Co's 90,000-bpd crude unit maintenance until March 21.
Traders said physical gas oil would continue to get good support at $25.00 per barrel.

India's purchase of an additional three cargoes of gas oil for April was largely ignored as this was within market expectations. India has already purchased 570,000 tonnes in an earlier tender for April.
India has also issued three term tenders to buy 1.0, 0.5 and 0.25 percent sulphur gas oil, as well as kerosene for May 1997-April 1998 deliveries.

Three buyers emerged with higher physical bids -- two European majors and a trader -- at between $25.40 and $25.60 per barrel for second-half March lifting fob. Sellers were holding out for higher prices.
On Friday, gas oil was traded at $25.00 for a March 22-26 lifting cargo fob.
The swaps March/April spread is now around 90 cents per barrel but traders expect it to top $1.00 soon.

The limited prompt jet fuel supplies have forced prices upward. The high prices were also spurred by a local trader seeking to price its sales into Indonesia. The trader has bought about 55,000 tonnes of jet fuel over the past month.

The trader on Monday bought 100,000 barrels of jet at $28.50 a barrel for March 18-22 lifting fob from a European major. A Japanese trader was also offering at $28.20 but for a later date--end March/early April--which faced no bids.
A bid was seen on Friday at $27.50 for March 18-22.
Taiwan was expected to issue a jet fuel import tender this week for April delivery, a CPC source said.
Jet fuel's strength was reflected in the widening jet/gas oil regrade when it was last bid at $1.90 a barrel for March, compared with Friday's indications of $1.40./$1.80.
